name: King Polemo of Pontus
bio: King Polemo of Pontus is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors dates the poet to 1st century BC. Paton's index describes him as a king of Pontus.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the third volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book IX: 746).

poems.title: Book IX, 746: On a Ring
poems.author: King Polemo of Pontus
poems.text: This little jasper stone has a seal of seven cows looking like one, and all looking at us as if alive. Perhaps the cows would have run away, but now the little herd is confined in the golden pen.

poems.title: Book XI, 38
poems.author: King Polemo of Pontus
poems.note: Paton’s heading: “On a relief representing a jar, a loaf, a crown, and a skull”.
poems.text: This is the poor man’s welcome armour against hunger—a jar and a loaf, here is a crown of dewy leaves, and this is the holy bone, outwork of a dead brain, the highest citadel of the soul. “ Drink,’ says the sculpture, “and eat, and surround thee with flowers, for like to this we suddenly become.”
